logline: A villager kid wakes to a torch on every block of his village and decides something big is coming, but the last growing row leads to his own door, where his best friend, the village's only player, places the final torch on the spot he lit every night, waves, and walks away without his nightly 'see you tomorrow'.
question: why tf did someone put 6,000 torches on this village overnight?
premise: One morning a plains village wakes with a torch on every grass block, fence post, roof ridge and hay bale: six thousand of them, when one torch would light a whole yard. The baby villager who tells it decides something big must be coming. Jonah, the village's only player and the kid's best friend, has put one torch by the kid's door every night, so the kid is never in the dark, and said 'see you tomorrow' before going home. Yesterday Jonah said he only had one last night, which the kid reads as Jonah being grounded again. This morning all of Jonah's things are in the kid's family chest and Jonah's house is gone, just torches. One row is still growing; the kid follows it to his own door.
twist: Nothing is coming: Jonah is going. He only had one last night in this world (he is leaving the game for good), so he spent it doing every night's torch at once, a torch on every block so his friend is never in the dark (the gesture, in the kid's own words from L06; nothing claims mobs stop spawning forever). He took his house down, gave everything he owned to the kid's family, and saved the nightly spot by the kid's door for the last torch. He places it, waves, and walks away, and this time he doesn't say 'see you tomorrow'.
